available.statement: For every elliptic curve E/Q, the abelian group E(Q) is finitely generated.
available.hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve overQ.
available.normalizations: The full rational-points group, with its finite torsion subgroup.
available.limit_order: Fix E/Q; the theorem gives finite generation, not generators or an effective rank bound.

needed: For the actual full-rational-two-torsion E/Q, dim_F2 E(Q)/2E(Q)=r+2.
derivation: Write E(Q)=Z^r plus a finite abelian torsion group T. Multiplication by2 on finite T has equal kernel and cokernel sizes, so dim T/2T=dim T[2]=2 by full rational two-torsion. Hence the required dimension is r+2.
boundary: No analytic-rank equality or finiteness of Sha is inferred.

available_assertion.statement: The finite all-place Kummer and Selmer sequences identify the rational-points, Selmer and Sha-torsion terms.
available_assertion.objects: Finite Kummer and all-place Selmer groups of A/Q at powers of two.
available_assertion.hypotheses: A is an elliptic curve over Q; finite multiplication-by-2^n sequences with all local conditions.
available_assertion.quantifiers: Every actual elliptic curve A/Q satisfying the stated hypotheses.
available_assertion.parameter_range: Positive integers n; finite powers of two.
available_assertion.uniformity: Qualitative statement for each A; no effective bound.
available_assertion.constants: No numerical constant or effective bound.
available_assertion.normalizations: Finite sequences only. The filtered direct limit and corank computation are separate local deductions.
available_assertion.exceptional_cases: Includes prime two; does not itself supply finite Sha, rank equality or Mordell–Weil finite generation.
available_assertion.limit_order: Fix each finite power first; direct-limit passage is supplied separately.

derivation: At n=1 use exact0→E(Q)/2E(Q)→Sel2(E/Q)→Sha(E/Q)[2]→0 with the all-place local conditions. Insert the separately obtained dimension r+2 and the hypothesis dim Sel2=3. This proves finite Sha[2] of dimension at most1; it does not prove finiteness of the whole Sha group.

needed: For A=Sha(E/Q)[2∞] with dim A[2]<=1, A=(Q2/Z2)^t plus a finite group F; the divisible summand is maximal and dim A[2]=t+dim F[2].
derivation: If A[2]=0 then A=0, since any nonzero2-power-torsion element has a nonzero multiple of order2. Otherwise |A[2]|=2. Inductively the multiplication-by2 map A[2^n]→A[2^(n-1)] has kernel of size2, so |A[2^n]|<=2^n and every A[2^n] is finite. A finite subgroup H of A has at most one nonzero element of order2. Choose an element of maximal order2^e in H; since H=H[2^e], the same kernel count gives |H|<=2^e, so this element generates H. Thus every A[2^n] is cyclic. If element orders in A are bounded by2^e, A=A[2^e] is finite cyclic: take t=0,F=A. If orders are unbounded, for each n an element of order at least2^n gives |A[2^n]|>=2^n, hence A[2^n] is cyclic of exact order2^n. Multiplication by2 from the next cyclic group onto it is surjective. Choose compatible generators inductively; their union identifies A with Q2/Z2. Then take t=1,F=0. These cases prove the displayed decomposition under the actual already established rank bound without a general cofinite-generation theorem. In either case any divisible subgroup has zero image in finite F, so the displayed summand is maximal. Taking2-torsion of the direct sum gives the claimed dimension identity.
incoming: A is the2-primary torsion subgroup by definition.
The previous finite Kummer calculation gives dim_F2 A[2]<=1.
boundary: Before the separate alternating nondegenerate pairing is used, the finite cyclic F is not asserted to vanish. F=0 would still allow a nonzero divisible Sha subgroup; no finiteness of full Sha is claimed.
